title: Risk-first vertical positioning playbook
summary: A compact, sales-friendly playbook that centers messaging around risk, trust surface, and operational guarantees for five priority verticals: fintech, healthcare, legal, enterprise SaaS, and gov/defense. Purpose-built to help SDRs/AE/SEs run 30–60 day pilots and to frame product differentiation against inference incumbents and cloud providers.
positioning_framework: Risk-first framework: 1) Identify the customer’s top operational risk (data leakage, compliance, uptime, unpredictable cost, model regressions). 2) Map Redwood controls that reduce that risk (private deployments, SLAs, fallbacks, local KMS, verification pipelines). 3) Quantify the residual risk and business impact. 4) Offer a short pilot with explicit acceptance criteria and rollback triggers.
fintech_messaging:
Core claim: Predictable inference economics + provable isolation for money-handling applications. Key points:
- Value props: token-cost predictability, dedicated pools for PII separation, per-transaction latency SLOs, cryptographic key custody options.
- Proof points: Dedicated capacity benchmarks (99.9% tail latency under Xms for payments flow), audit log integration with Splunk/Datadog, early customers in payments and wealth.
- Sales objections and rebuttals: 'We can just use Managed Cloud A.' -> Rebuttal: Cloud providers offer models but not token-level cost visibility+fallback policies; Redwood ties per-route spend to token breakdowns and automated fallback to lower-cost variants with no schema change. 'Data residency requirements' -> Rebuttal: Private deployment + VPC option and HSM integration.
- Pilot ask: 30-day sandbox with one payments workflow (auth + receipt generation), measure cost per processed request and tail-latency percentiles. Acceptance: <= target cost delta and <2x baseline p99 latency.
healthcare_messaging:
Core claim: Clinical-grade inference with auditability and data governance. Key points:
- Value props: On-prem/private control plane, HIPAA-adjacent audit trails, model pinning + versioned rollouts to avoid regressions in clinical outputs.
- Proof points: Logging schema that maps inputs to model version + embeddings, integration pattern for EHR connectors, recommended evals for hallucination detection in clinical prompts.
- Sales objections and rebuttals: 'We need audited explainability' -> Rebuttal: Structured output plus traceable prompt/eval pipeline and differential testing of model deltas. 'We can't risk wrong clinical suggestions' -> Rebuttal: Deploy with conservative guardrails, human-in-loop triage, and synthetic/regression testing tied to release gate.
- Pilot ask: Proof-of-concept on one non-critical clinical assistant pathway (triage notes summarization). Acceptance: measurable reduction in triage time, no critical hallucinations across evaluation set.
legal_messaging:
Core claim: Confidential legal workflows served in-customer or in-isolated cloud with provable access controls. Key points:
- Value props: Data isolation, audit trails, fine-grained role authorization, legal-specific redaction templates and deterministic prompt templates.
- Proof points: Customer reference (early-stage lawtech partner) using private deployment with role-based access to contracts, examples of redaction accuracy and retention policies.
- Sales objections and rebuttals: 'We require absolute confidentiality' -> Rebuttal: Provide on-prem option + KMS/HSM and minimal metadata storage; show SOC2 and configurable retention. 'Model accuracy concerns' -> Rebuttal: Offer canary rollouts and A/B diffing of outputs with side-by-side judge harness.
- Pilot ask: 45-day pilot ingesting non-sensitive contract samples for clause extraction and redaction templates. Acceptance: F1 > threshold on extraction, clear retention policy implemented.
saas_messaging:
Core claim: Reduce unit inference cost and accelerate feature velocity for product teams while preserving SLAs. Key points:
- Value props: Autoscaling dedicated capacity for bursty usage, intelligent batching suggestions from Redwood Optimize, per-route cost attribution to product features.
- Proof points: Benchmarks showing 20–40% cost reduction with batching+prefix caching on typical in-app chat flows; console dashboards tying cost to feature flags.
- Sales objections and rebuttals: 'We can horizontally scale our own infra' -> Rebuttal: Building inference ops (kernels, quantization, KV cache) is expensive and brittle; Redwood provides validated kernels and autoscaler policies tuned to model and workload. 'We need multi-tenant isolation' -> Rebuttal: Dedicated capacity contracts and logical tenancy with quotas.
- Pilot ask: 30-day pilot with a single chat feature, instrumentation for cost per session. Acceptance: cost reduction target met and integration with product observability hooks.
govdef_messaging:
Core claim: Certified pathways for high-trust deployments with explicit control over compute locality, attestation, and SLA-backed uptime. Key points:
- Value props: Private control plane, air-gapped deployment options, FIPS/KMS integrations, prioritized incident response and compliance packaging.
- Proof points: Deployment runbook for air-gapped sites, example checklist for DoD/CIV partners, tailored breach notifications and contractual SLAs.
- Sales objections and rebuttals: 'We must vet every component' -> Rebuttal: Offer a technical deep-dive and supply chain documentation; provide on-prem build artifacts for review. 'We cannot accept external telemetry' -> Rebuttal: Configurable telemetry retention and local-only observability.
- Pilot ask: 60-day accredited lab integration with an allowed use-case (e.g., secure doc summarization). Acceptance: successful end-to-end deployment and passing of targeted compliance checklist.
competitive_notes:
High-level competitive map and counterplays:
- Cloud providers (CP): Strength = convenience + billing/marketplace channels. Weakness = limited per-token visibility, slower fallbacks, and not inference-optimized kernels. Counterplay: Lead with cost attribution, fallbacks, and runtime optimizations that CP marketplace bundles don't show.
- LLM API incumbents: Strength = broad model catalog and brand. Weakness = one-size-fits-all SLAs and limited private deployment options. Counterplay: Emphasize deterministic rollouts, private control plane, and SLO guarantees.
- Self-hosted inference stacks: Strength = control. Weakness = engineering lift and operational risk. Counterplay: Position Redwood as 'managed ops for inference' — same control, less build/ops overhead.
- Niche vertical vendors (healthcare-lawtech): Strength = domain fit. Weakness = narrow offering and scaling. Counterplay: Bundle domain starter kits (redaction templates, clinical evals) while keeping the platform open for custom integrations.
recommended_playbook:
Outbound + pilot playbook (for AEs/SEs):
1) Discovery checklist with risk quantifiers: data sensitivity level, uptime SLOs needed, cost tolerance, approval cycle length.
2) Quickwin pilot designs (30/45/60 days) per vertical with explicit acceptance criteria and rollback triggers.
3) Sales collateral: one-pager 'Risk Surface Map' per vertical (data flows, threats, controls).
4) Field enablement: 90-min SE workshop + runbook template for private deployments.
5) Post-pilot: transition plan to either Dedicated contract or Private onboarding; include post-mortem and remaining risk remediation items.

notes_to_self: Keep messaging honest: call out where Redwood cannot remove business risk (e.g., incorrect business logic from prompts) and pair with mitigations (human review, conservative model selection). Avoid overpromising certifications in a pilot stage. Use pilot pricing as a conversion lever.
